## This run specifically

Implement GitHub issue #22 — "A chat stuck on thinking cannot be cleared without a server restart".
https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/22

Nothing an operator can reach clears a chat sitting at `chat_sessions.status = 'thinking'`: the thread refuses new messages, the composer is disabled, and the only code that can move that row is `reconcileChatsOnBoot`, which runs once per process at boot.

Done looks like: an operator can recover a stuck thread without restarting the server, the recovery is safe when the turn is in fact still running (it must not silently abandon a live child), and there is a regression test that fails before the change and passes after. Every acceptance-criteria box in the issue holds.

Scope note: this is the recovery path. Issues #19 and #20 — which prevent two specific ways a turn gets stranded in the first place — are separate open issues and may be running in parallel on their own branches against the same `runTurn` in `src/lib/chat.ts`. Do not also fix those; build the recovery so it works regardless of whether they have landed, keep the diff minimal, and say in your report if you needed to touch shared code.
finalText:
Committed as `8e6a437`.

## What changed

A `chat_sessions` row stuck on `thinking` now has two ways out, neither of which depends on the child's `close` event:

- **`cancelChatTurn`** (`src/lib/chat.ts:718`) behind `POST /api/chat/[id]/cancel` and a **Stop** button beside Send. It signals the live child on `interruptRun`'s SIGINT→SIGTERM→SIGKILL ladder and returns `signalled` vs `cleared`, mirroring `stopRun`.
- **A 30s sweeper** (`sweepStuckChats`, `src/lib/chat.ts:751`) that fails out any `thinking` row past `CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS + 60s`. Lazily started when a turn begins, stopped when none is left.

Both settle the row themselves, so `finishTurn` now latches on `WHERE status='thinking'` — a late `close` changes nothing rather than reviving the thread. `turn_started_at` is a new nullable column, not a read of `updated_at`, because the chat's own `save_template` tool appends a system message mid-turn and would push the deadline out by however long the turn had already run.

**Shared code touched:** `runTurn` gained three lines (register the child after spawn, drop it in `land`, use the shared timeout string). No logic in the spawn or parse path moved, so #19/#20 should merge either way.

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | How checked |
|---|---|
| Recoverable from the page without a restart | Stop button → `POST /api/chat/[id]/cancel` → `cancelChatTurn` writes `status='failed'` unconditionally on a `thinking` row. Read through, not exercised in a browser. |
| A live child is signalled, not orphaned | `turns` map registers the child immediately after `spawn`; `endTurn` signals the tree. Diverges from `interruptRun` in re-checking `child.exitCode`/`signalCode` rather than map identity, because the operator can send a new message — registering a new child under the same id — while the old one is mid-ladder. |
| Timeout enforced independently of `close` | `sweepStuckChats` reads the row only. |
| Error distinguishes the two causes | `CANCELLED_REASON` / `TIMED_OUT_REASON`, written to `error` and appended to the thread. |
| Regression test failing before, passing after | Confirmed both directions — see below. |

## Verification

```
NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev   ok
npm run typecheck                            ok (exit 0, no output)
npm test                                     225 pass, 0 fail, 38 suites
npm run build                                FAILS — pre-existing
```

The regression test, both directions:

- **Before:** `git stash push src/lib/chat.ts src/lib/db.ts` → `npm test` fails to compile with 11 errors (`Module './chat' has no exported member 'staleTurn'`, `'turn_started_at' does not exist in type 'Partial<ChatRow>'`).
- **Assertions are load-bearing**, not just the import — I patched three plausible wrong implementations into the shipped `staleTurn` and each broke distinct cases: dropping the `status` check → 1 failure; reading `updated_at` instead of `turn_started_at` → 2; inverting the comparison → 3. Source restored and byte-compared against the pre-patch copy afterwards.

**`npm run build` fails and it is not my change.** `> Build error occurred [TypeError: generate is not a function]`, with no stack even under `--debug`. I stashed everything including untracked files, confirmed a clean tree at `9e0cd6e`, and got the identical failure. It reproduces with and without `NODE_ENV=development`. Environment (arm64 Linux, node v22.23.2), not code. A human should run `npm run build` and `docker compose up --build` on a working host — the issue's verification block names both, and I could run neither Docker nor a browser here.

## Not verified

No real CLI child was signalled, and no sweep fired against a live row. Both are recorded in the README's *Not yet verified by hand* list, with the two things to watch and a `sqlite3` recipe that exercises the no-child half of each without spending anything.

## Noticed, left alone

`sendChatMessage`'s `void runTurn(...).catch(...)` does not catch a *synchronous* throw from `runTurn` — `writeMcpConfig` throws before the promise exists, so the rejection surfaces on `sendChatMessage` instead and the row is left `thinking` with no child. That is issue #19/#20's territory. The recovery path handles the resulting stranded row regardless of whether they land.

DONE
